papers.title: Effects of carbonization temperature on the performance of bamboo fiber-reinforced cementitious composites and their potential applications in deicing pavement
papers.authors: Chunpeng Liu, Feifei Zhang, Yong Luo, Xinyu Wan, Ren Wei, Dianah Mazlan, Tze Liang Lau
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and chloride penetration of bamboo fiber-reinforced cementitious composites for potential deicing pavement applications.
papers.methods: Bamboo fibers were incorporated at dosages of 1.5%–4.5% in three states (uncarbonized, carbonized at 300 °C, and carbonized at 800 °C). Compressive strength, splitting tensile strength, thermal conductivity, rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response before and after dry-wet cycling, microstructural characteristics, and scenario-based finite element analysis were evaluated.
papers.results: Uncarbonized fibers improved tensile resistance but reduced thermal conductivity. The 800 °C carbonized bamboo-derived material enhanced thermal conductivity, exhibited lower RCPT charge-passed values, and showed a carbon-rich structure with a denser fiber-matrix interface (e.g., a 19% increase in thermal conductivity at 3.5% fiber content relative to the reference mixture). Finite element analysis showed that lowering ambient temperature from -3 to -8 °C increased heating time from 2.6 to 3.4 h.
papers.keywords: bamboo fiber, carbonization temperature, cementitious composites, thermal conductivity, deicing pavement, finite element analysis
papers.citation_apa: Liu, C., Zhang, F., Luo, Y., Wan, X., Wei, R., Mazlan, D., & Lau, T. L. (2026). papers.title: Olivine-hosted spinel–diopside symplectic intergrowths in Eoarchean dunites: Records of dehydrogenation-oxidation of a hydrous precursor
papers.authors: Juan Miguel Guotana, Yumiko Harigane, Ikuya Nishio, Akihiro Tamura, Tomoyuki Mizukami, Kenichiro Tani, Pedro Waterton, Kristoffer Szilas, Keita Itano, Tomoaki Morishita
papers.summary: This study examines olivine from an Eoarchean dunite lens in the Isua Supracrustal Belt, Greenland, which hosts fine-scale spinel-diopside symplectic intergrowths. The researchers analyze these textures using electron backscatter diffraction and mineral chemistry to infer that they formed via the dehydrogenation and oxidation of a hydrous olivine precursor, providing evidence for structurally-bound hydrogen in Earth's early mantle.
papers.methods: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) mapping, mineral composition analysis (electron microprobe), and first-order stoichiometric estimation based on mineral oxidation and hydrogen release.
papers.results: The olivine hosts fine-scale Cr-magnetite and diopside symplectic intergrowths exhibiting a strong topotaxial relationship with the host olivine [(100) Ol //{111} Spl ]. Based on crystallographic orientation, trace Ti amounts, and absence of ilmenite, hydrous olivine is identified as the precursor phase. A first-order stoichiometric estimate yields approximately 10 ppm H in the precursor phase, recording a closed-system, high-temperature solid-state replacement process.
papers.keywords: Eoarchean dunite, symplectic intergrowths, hydrous olivine, dehydrogenation, Isua Supracrustal Belt, topotaxial relationship

papers.summary: This paper investigates the transport characteristics of hybrid nanofluids incorporating multiple nanoparticles under the influence of Joule heating, magnetic field effects, and thermal radiation over a vertically stretched surface, utilizing an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) computational framework.
papers.methods: Formulation of a physical model for coupled momentum and heat transfer, conversion of governing nonlinear equations into a dimensionless mathematical system using similarity transformations and thermophysical relations, and computational investigation via an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) framework.
papers.results: Stretching of the surface intensifies fluid motion, whereas the Hartman number opposes flow and reduces velocity distribution. Stronger Joule heating, radiation, and Eckert number effects enhance the thermal distribution, and nanoparticle concentration in the range of 0.1% to 0.4% benefits the heat mechanism.

papers.title: Thermodynamically Constrained Deep Learning for Hydrogen Sorption Prediction: Overcoming Classical Isotherm Generalization Failure through Physics-Informed Cross-Lithology Transferability
papers.authors: Mohammad Nooraiepour, Mohammad Masoudi, Zezhang Song, Helge Hellevang
papers.summary: The paper presents a thermodynamics-informed, physics-regularized neural network framework to predict hydrogen sorption in fine-grained geological materials, aiming to overcome the generalization failure of classical isotherm models across heterogeneous populations.
papers.methods: The framework uses a seven-category physics-informed feature engineering scheme generating 62 thermodynamically meaningful descriptors, a multiterm loss function enforcing saturation limits and monotonic pressure responses via penalty weights, an architecture-diverse ten-member ensemble with post hoc temperature-scaling calibration, and a three-phase curriculum training strategy incorporating Van't Hoff temperature dependence.
papers.results: On a random-split holdout set, the framework achieves R2 = 0.9544, RMSE = 0.0484 mmol/g, MAE = 0.0231 mmol/g, a 98.6% monotonicity satisfaction rate, and zero negative predictions. Under leave-one-lithology-out (LOLO) validation, it retains R2 = 0.723 for coal and 0.794 for shale, outperforming a random forest baseline.
papers.keywords: physics-informed neural networks, hydrogen sorption, thermodynamics, geological materials, cross-lithology generalization

papers.summary: This study investigates reaction-driven fracturing and ultramafic rock weakening induced by CO2 mineralization by exposing serpentinized dunite samples to Mg(OH)2-brine at 90°C and 3.5 MPa for up to 32 days.

papers.results: Tensile microfractures nucleated within 11 days and progressed to core disaggregation, with localized damage concentrated along pre-existing veins and flaw tips. papers.title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
papers.authors: Siva Viknesh, Amirhossein Arzani
papers.summary: The paper develops an overlapping Schwarz domain-decomposition framework based on perturbation theory for high-Péclet-number transport problems with thin boundary layers. It integrates differentiable physics solvers with agentic AI optimization and large language models (LLMs) to perform inverse modeling where governing equations are imposed as hard constraints.
papers.methods: An overlapping Schwarz domain-decomposition framework grounded in perturbation theory using an inner equation for near-wall dynamics and an outer equation for bulk transport, discretized using the finite element method. A fully differentiable multidomain physics solver is assembled, and large language models (LLMs) / agentic AI are integrated into the inverse workflow to propose parameter updates and grow a library of candidate basis functions during optimization.
papers.results: The formulation permits coarser mesh resolutions and reduces computational cost relative to a single-domain formulation. The agentic AI configuration is shown to be most advantageous when the spatially varying unknown is represented in a functional basis, with the AI agent growing the library of candidate basis functions in stages and initializing their parameters.
papers.keywords: Schwarz domain-decomposition, boundary layer transport, finite element method, differentiable physics, inverse modeling, agentic AI, LLM optimization

papers.title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
papers.authors: Krishan Chand, Ahmad Peyvan, Haoxiang Luo
papers.summary: The paper investigates the influence of non-dimensionalization on the trainability and accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) applied to buoyancy-driven flows, using a differentially heated square cavity.
papers.methods: The study uses a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10^3–10^5 to compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall velocity scalings under identical training conditions, and performs direct gradient measurements to analyze coefficient-induced gradient imbalances.
papers.results: The free-fall scaling achieves errors below 1.1% in the mean Nusselt number for Ra <= 10^4, whereas the diffusive scaling produces errors of 157–650% and diverges at Ra = 10^5 due to a coefficient-induced gradient imbalance scaling as (Ra*Pr)^2. Sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting do not resolve the training difficulties, and for unsteady convection, the free-fall PINN fails to capture the transient Nusselt-number overshoot.
papers.limitations: Tested specifically for buoyancy-driven flows in a differentially heated square cavity under certain Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers; sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting failed to resolve training difficulties under the tested conditions.
papers.keywords: physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), buoyancy-driven flow, non-dimensionalization, gradient imbalance, heat transfer

papers.summary: The paper examines data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for steady, two-dimensional incompressible flow in a deep lid-driven cavity (depth-to-width ratio of five) at Reynolds numbers 100, 250, 500, and 1000, using a hard-constrained streamfunction formulation combined with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants.
papers.methods: Evaluation using a hard-constrained streamfunction formulation combined with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants on a deep lid-driven cavity flow at Reynolds numbers 100, 250, 500, and 1000, compared against independent spectral/hp calculations.

At Re=1000 on a 161x801 assessment, a refined workflow lowered interior velocity discrepancy to 2.658% and gauge-aligned pressure RMS discrepancy to 1.167x10^-3 ρU^2.

papers.title: Heat transfer and flow in MgO-water and TiO2-water nanofluids in rectangular cavities: Role of aspect ratio and thermal efficiency
papers.authors: Tohid Adibi, Saeed Soltani, Haleh Jafarzadeh, Nemat Mashoofi Maleki, Amir Keshmiri
papers.summary: This paper numerically investigates laminar mixed convection of MgO-water and TiO2-water nanofluids in lid-driven rectangular cavities with varying aspect ratios at a constant Reynolds number, analyzing heat transfer, flow structure, and thermal efficiency.
papers.methods: Numerical simulation using an in-house finite-volume Fortran code with a second-order characteristics-based scheme to solve governing equations for nanofluids (phi = 2%) at Re = 100 across aspect ratios of 0.5, 1, 2, 4, and 8.
papers.results: Flow structure transitions from two counter-rotating vortices at high AR to a single dominant vortex at AR = 1, and to a boundary-layer-dominated regime at AR = 0.5. Pure water achieves max average Nusselt number (Nu = 16.40) at AR = 0.5, while MgO-water achieves its highest relative enhancement at AR = 8 (Nu = 5.28, 37% improvement) with a friction penalty of f_max = 4/AR. Thermal Efficiency Parameter (TEP) yields TEP > 1 for MgO-water only at AR = 8 (TEP = 1.06), is neutral at AR = 2, and detrimental elsewhere, while TiO2-water is neutral or detrimental at all AR.
papers.keywords: nanofluids, mixed convection, rectangular cavities, aspect ratio, thermal efficiency parameter, finite-volume method

papers.summary: This paper presents a lifecycle-oriented review of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in offshore wind geotechnical engineering, synthesizing research from 2001 to 2025 across site investigation, foundation design, installation, and operation and maintenance.
papers.methods: A systematically screened review of research articles published between 2001 and 2025 and selected project- and industry-level practices.
papers.results: Foundation design shows the highest research concentration, while digital ground modeling and design-stage surrogate analysis show the clearest pathways to engineering use. Closed-loop installation control and below-mudline state inference remain largely at the research or validation stage.
papers.limitations: Sparse offshore data, insufficient physical constraints, limited cross-site generalizability, incomplete standardization, and limited engineering acceptance.
papers.keywords: artificial intelligence, offshore wind, geotechnical engineering, lifecycle review, surrogate modeling

papers.title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
papers.authors: Ehsan Roohi, Christopher
papers.summary: The paper examines data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for steady, two-dimensional incompressible flow in a deep lid-driven cavity across various Reynolds numbers, focusing on regional accuracy and recirculation characteristics.
papers.methods: Employs data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combining an established hard-constrained streamfunction formulation with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants. Evaluated against independent spectral/hp calculations providing reference fields.
papers.results: For D/W = 5 and Re = 100, 250, 500, and 1000, interior velocity RMS discrepancies range from 6.542×10−3U to 9.541×10−3U, and gauge-aligned pressure RMS discrepancies range from 2.082×10−3ρU2 to 5.838×10−3ρU2. A refined workflow at Re = 1000 lowers interior velocity RMS discrepancy to 3.394×10−3U and pressure RMS discrepancy to 1.167×10−3ρU2.
papers.limitations: Configuration rankings depend on both region and observable, and localized rotational-field discrepancies remain substantial.
papers.keywords: physics-informed neural networks, PINNs, lid-driven cavity, computational fluid dynamics, fluid flow, recirculation
papers.citation_apa: Roohi, E., & Christopher (2026). Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity. https://doi.org/10.66977/xsci.2610.003l

papers.title: PHYSICS-CONSTRAINED NEURAL INTELLIGENCE: A MATHEMATICAL FRAMEWORK FOR UNIVERSE-GOVERNED NEURAL NETWORKS From Statistical Guesswork to Physical Understanding: How Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) Bridge the Gap Between Artificial Pattern Recognition and Genuine Scientific Comprehension
papers.authors: mohamed kamal arafa el-rakhawi
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: The paper introduces the El-Rakhawi Physics-Constrained Intelligence Framework, which embeds fundamental physics laws and PDEs into neural network learning architectures (PINNs) to bridge artificial pattern recognition and scientific comprehension.
papers.methods: The framework utilizes Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) that learn simultaneously from data and physical laws, featuring a generalized loss function for homogeneous and non-homogeneous PDEs, a logistic Physics Compliance Index (PCI) for bounding, and causal separation between structural compliance and data efficiency.
papers.results: The framework achieved a Data Efficiency (DEI) of 0.94 compared to 0.30 for traditional methods, an Interpretability (II) of 0.95 compared to 0.20 for black-box models, and a Unified Unified Physics-Constrained Intelligence Index (UPCII) of 0.95 with a zero-tolerance penalty.
papers.keywords: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), universe-governed neural networks, PDEs, conservation laws, physics compliance, mesh-free CFD

papers.title: Numerical Modeling of Solid–Liquid Phase‐Change Materials: A Critical Review of Formulations, Validation, and Application‐Oriented Model Selection
papers.authors: M. S. Kadiri, Jaouad Bahadi
papers.summary: This paper provides a critical review of numerical models for solid-liquid phase-change materials (PCMs), examining formulations, validation, and application-oriented model selection.
papers.methods: The study examines numerical models from three perspectives: benchmarking, parameter sensitivity, and application-oriented model selection, assessing various approaches (including enthalpy-based, enthalpy-porosity, effective heat-capacity, simplified conduction, sharp-interface, reduced-order, and data-driven methods) in terms of physical fidelity, computational cost, natural convection, interface representation, parameter sensitivity, and validation evidence.
papers.results: The analysis demonstrates that no single model is universally optimal; credible PCM simulation requires matching model complexity to the dominant physics, available validation observables, and intended engineering decisions. It also highlights the impact of the mushy-zone constant and explains why temperature-only comparisons are insufficient.
papers.keywords: phase-change materials, numerical modeling, enthalpy method, validation, benchmarking, data-driven approaches
papers.citation_apa: Kadiri, M. S., & Bahadi, J. (2026). Numerical Modeling of Solid–Liquid Phase‐Change Materials: A Critical Review of Formulations, Validation, and Application‐Oriented Model Selection. Heat Transfer. https://doi.org/10.1002/htj.70410

papers.title: Data-Driven Estimation of Ship Manoeuvring Hydrodynamic Derivatives using a Hybrid MARUS–PINN Framework with LLM-Guided Symbolic Discovery
papers.authors: Paria Rezayan, Konstantinos Domdouzis, Yogang Singh
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: This thesis investigates a hybrid framework combining MARUS-simulated maneuvering data, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and Large Language Model (LLM)-guided symbolic discovery to estimate ship maneuvering hydrodynamic derivatives for autonomous vessels, aiming to improve robustness, data efficiency, and interpretability compared to conventional methods.
papers.methods: The study uses a hybrid MARUS-PINN framework with LLM-guided symbolic discovery, utilizing Marine Robotics Unity Simulator (MARUS) data, PINN-based parameter learning, and experiments/ablation studies comparing the hybrid model with purely data-driven and purely physics-based counterparts across various USVs.
papers.results: Integrating symbolic discovery with PINNs reduces sway-acceleration error by 86%, yaw-rate acceleration error by 66%, and heading-rollout error by 89% relative to purely data-driven baselines, producing compact, physically consistent residual terms, while physics-only counterparts catastrophically diverge from ground-truths.
papers.keywords: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), ship maneuvering, hydrodynamic derivatives, symbolic discovery, Large Language Models (LLMs), computational fluid dynamics (CFD)
